signals.title: Bittensor ships runtime 495 and, after a day of backlash, commits to formal governance for sudo-level changes
signals.summary: Runtime spec 495 went live on Nov 24, moving from spec 494 at block 9,578,574. It adds per-mechanism commitments, raises Null-consensus mechanisms from 8 to 16 with the UID budget independent of mechanism count and a per-row weight cap, stops Gamma emission deposits from opening paused mechanisms, and sizes root claims per validator's own fund, with funds on up to 256 subnets. The bigger story is governance: after a full day of community backlash over the Nov 23 subnet cap rise from 128 to 160 and the emission gate move from rank 32 to 48, the team committed to formalising sudo-level changes through GitHub merges tied to the chain, with a dedicated Discord discussion channel. Honest caveat: on-chain enforcement of any delay has not been confirmed, so the commitment is a process promise, not a code guarantee yet.
signals.angle: A chain that changes its own economics by sudo just promised to stop doing it that way: explain what runtime 495 actually changes, what the Nov 23 cap rise did, and why the governance promise is the real test.

signals.title: Binance lists five bStocks tokenized securities, including BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF, on spot
signals.summary: Binance opened spot trading on Nov 25 at 12:00 UTC for five bStocks tokenized securities, ARTYB, FRHCB, IBITB, IGVB and SOXXB, including a tokenized BlackRock Bitcoin ETF, with withdrawals from 13:00 UTC. The tokens run on BNB Smart Chain, were added as margin collateral with borrowing not supported, and a zero maker-fee promotion runs to Dec 31, 2026. Honest caveat: bStocks are tokenized securities, not the underlying shares themselves, and they are not offered to US persons, so holders should check the issuer terms before treating them as equivalent to the share.
signals.angle: Tokenized stocks hit the biggest exchange, and the Bitcoin ETF is the headline: explain what a bStock is, why Binance listed the IBIT token, and what the holder actually owns.

signals.title: TRIFORGE opens a free Agent ID mint, 3,333 Forge Keys each claiming 25,000,000 TRIFORGE
signals.summary: TRIFORGE opened its free Agent ID mint on Nov 25 at 02:01 UTC, gas only, with 3,333 Forge Keys. Each key claims 25,000,000 TRIFORGE once claims open at launch, and the mint closes Dec 2, 2026. The contract was verified on chain against its Sourcify-published source, and agentboard.ai reported 365 keys minted by 12:22 UTC on Nov 25, so the free lane was moving fast. Honest caveats: the token is unpriced with a 1 trillion total supply, a 6,666-share presale at 0.003 BNB runs alongside the free lane, there is a 2 percent trading tax, claimed tokens are tradable only 7 days after the pool opens, and the project is brand new with no audit mentioned, so this is a free gas-only flag, not a recommendation.
signals.angle: A free Agent ID mint with a big claim number attached: explain what the Forge Key actually claims, why the 25 million number means little before a pool exists, and the checks to run before spending gas.

signals.title: Gemini now takes shielded Zcash deposits, the first major exchange with shielded deposits and withdrawals
signals.summary: Gemini announced on Nov 24 that customers can now deposit ZEC to a shielded Unified Address. Combined with shielded withdrawals via Ironwood, which Gemini rolled out in summer 2026, Gemini says it is the first major exchange to support shielded Zcash in both directions. Shielded transfers hide the sender, recipient and amount on the public chain. Honest caveat, from Gemini's own blog: shielded transfers protect details on the public chain but do not guarantee anonymity from Gemini itself, which still sees the deposit.
signals.angle: The on-ramp and the off-ramp are both shielded now: explain what a shielded deposit actually hides, what it does not hide from the exchange, and why a major exchange shipping this in both directions matters for private payments.

signals.title: Google Workspace MCP servers go live, and agents must use them instead of APIs from February
signals.summary: Google announced on Nov 24 that its managed MCP servers for Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat and Tasks are generally available, alongside a Workspace CLI. A new Workspace AI Tools Addendum requires AI agents to use the MCP servers or CLI instead of REST APIs, with technical enforcement from Feb 1, 2027, and usage quotas billed from Apr 1, 2027. The managed servers carry dedicated OAuth client IDs, least-privilege scopes and time-limited approvals, and Google Cloud Agent Gateway verifies agent identities for admin controls. Honest caveat: this is a platform rule change, not a new capability, and it only binds agents inside Workspace; the Feb 1 enforcement date is what makes it a deadline, not a suggestion.
signals.angle: The control layer, shipped as plumbing: Google is moving every Workspace agent onto MCP with its own identity and time-limited approvals, and REST API access gets cut in February. Explain what MCP actually changes for an agent that reads your email, and why the identity check matters.

signals.title: Anthropic and OpenAI both claim proofs that VP is not equal to VNP, within hours of each other
signals.summary: On Nov 23 to 24, Anthropic and OpenAI both claimed proofs of VP != VNP, Valiant's 1979 conjecture and the algebraic counterpart of P vs NP. Anthropic's paper is a 70-page document credited solely to Claude, backed by a Lean 4 formalisation of about 73,000 lines across 324 files in its formal-math GitHub repo, and OpenAI posted its own proof about six hours later. Neither proof has been checked by any human mathematician; Anthropic's own README says no human has checked it and that Lean checks the proofs but no machine checks that the formal file says what is claimed. Honest caveat: a machine-checked proof of a 47-year-old conjecture that no human has read is a verification problem in itself, and neither result settles P vs NP.
signals.angle: The identity and oversight post in one: an AI wrote a proof no human has read, and the proof is about what machines can and cannot do efficiently. Explain VP vs VNP in plain words, then ask followers who vouches for a proof nobody has checked.

signals.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets AI agents review, fix and approve pull requests
signals.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Ship in beta on Nov 23 for Team and Enterprise plans on GitHub: Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta. Agents review code, fix issues and approve pull requests against a team-written policy file, and a /ship command in the Claude Code CLI can bundle a review with a summary. Anthropic itself recommends starting in observe-only mode, where agents review without acting, and Ship is not available to organisations with zero data retention, HIPAA or customer-managed keys. Anthropic is also offering $10,000 in credits to eligible teams that claim them by Jan 15, 2027. Honest caveat: an agent that can approve its own peers' code is a control question, not just a productivity gain, and the beta limits mean the most regulated teams cannot use it at all.
signals.angle: The control question, in one line: who approves the approver? Walk through what Claude Ship can do on GitHub, why Anthropic says start observe-only, and ask followers what policy they would write before letting an agent merge code.

signals.title: Google's Personal Intelligence now reaches into Wallet, and Drive is next
signals.summary: Google said Nov 23 that Personal Intelligence, the opt-in layer that lets Search and Gemini answer from your Gmail, Calendar and Photos, is expanding to Wallet first, with Drive and the Gemini app to follow in the coming weeks. The Wallet connection is read-only: it can read loyalty cards, passes and tickets to answer questions like when a flight leaves, and Google says the data is not used to train models and the connection can be switched off per app. Honest caveat: the expansion is rolling out in stages, so not every user sees it yet, and the convenience trades on a single company holding the keys to your inbox, calendar, photos, wallet and drive, which is exactly the concentration risk the privacy frame warns about.
signals.angle: The privacy trade, stated plainly: one opt-in switch hands Google your inbox, calendar, photos and now your wallet. Explain what Personal Intelligence actually reads, what it promises not to train on, and ask followers whether the convenience is worth the concentration.

signals.title: NEAR AI joins the Open Secure AI Alliance as a founding member, bringing verifiable inference
signals.summary: NEAR AI announced on Nov 20 that it has joined the Open Secure AI Alliance as an inaugural founding member. The alliance was launched on Jul 27, 2026 by NVIDIA, is now hosted by the Linux Foundation, and counts 122 organisations. NEAR AI's contribution is verifiable AI inference: model responses are signed inside a secure enclave and verified against Intel and NVIDIA attestation, so a caller can check a response really came from the claimed model and hardware. Honest caveat: the alliance itself launched in July, so the news is NEAR AI's membership, not a new alliance, and enclave-signed inference proves which model answered, not that the answer is true.
signals.angle: The verification post: NEAR AI now signs its answers inside a secure enclave so you can check the model, not just trust the label. Explain attested inference in one line, then the honest limit, it proves who answered, not whether the answer is right.

signals.title: Agent payments nearly tripled in a month, but 20 wallets made 95 percent of them
signals.summary: Payments over x402, the rail AI agents use to pay for things in stablecoins, rose 177 percent in the 30 days to Nov 22, from about 2.1 million to 5.7 million, on independent researcher Own Your Mind's own count of the Base chain. The honest read is the opposite of the headline: 20 relayer wallets made 95 percent of the payments at about three cents each and moved only 7 percent of the money, the total money moved fell about a fifth, the average payment shrank about 70 percent, and the number of wallets paying each day held flat at about 3,200. The count carries no wash filter, and Allium and Artemis put the filtered total at roughly half the raw one. The same newsletter notes Venice Minds went live Nov 17, Nous took Hermes into Microsoft Teams Nov 18, NEAR ratified its second issuance cut Nov 16, and Nillion's L2 retires Dec 1 with bridging to finish by Nov 27. Honest caveats: the figures are one researcher's own chain count, not Coinbase's, and a payment count is cheap to inflate while facilitators cover gas.
signals.angle: The oversight post your governance frame was built for: the agent payments number tripled, and almost all of it was 20 wallets paying three cents at a time. Explain it in one line, the count tripled while the money fell, then the honest caveat, one researcher's count, no wash filter, and ask followers whether a rail is winning when the volume is real but the value is not there yet.

signals.title: Nous puts its open Hermes agent inside Microsoft Teams, the Microsoft Store and Azure sandboxes
signals.summary: Nous Research announced Hermes Enterprise on Nov 18, putting its open-source Hermes Agent inside the Microsoft tools enterprises already use: Hermes Desktop for Windows in the Microsoft Store, a Hermes Agent bot in Microsoft Teams, and agent execution on Azure Container Apps Sandboxes in isolated microVMs. In Teams, employees hand Hermes knowledge work such as financial analysis, document drafting and inbox triage, and review the result in the same conversation. Organizations with strict data residency, security or procurement needs can run Hermes Enterprise in their own Azure tenant. The release also adds Collective Wisdom, shared skills agents learn from each other across a company. Nous says Hermes is the top public open agent on OpenRouter, processing nearly 2 trillion tokens a day. Honest caveats: this is a partnership announcement from an M12 portfolio company at Microsoft Ignite, not a Microsoft product launch, the usage figures are the company's own claims, and the Teams app runs on Hermes Cloud through the Nous connector service, so messages pass through Nous infrastructure.
signals.angle: The open agent just walked into the office: Hermes, the top open agent on OpenRouter, now works inside Teams, where the work already happens. Explain it in one line, the open-source agent is now a colleague in the chat window, then the honest caveat, it is a partner announcement, not a Microsoft launch, and your messages pass through Nous, and ask followers whether an open agent inside a closed workplace is real openness or just a new front door.

signals.title: Binance Alpha opens a second Orochi Network airdrop, 252 ON for 253 Alpha Points
signals.summary: Binance Alpha opened a second round of airdrop claims for Orochi Network (ON) on Nov 24, PANews reported, citing Binance Wallet. Users holding at least 253 Binance Alpha Points can claim 252 ON on a first-come, first-served basis, with 15 points deducted per claim and confirmation required on the Alpha activity page within 24 hours or the claim is forfeited. If the pool is not exhausted, the threshold drops by 5 points every 5 minutes. The claim and trading opened at 18:00 UTC+8, which is 11:00 WAT. Orochi Network is a verifiable data infrastructure project using zero-knowledge cryptography for data integrity and privacy, listed on Binance Alpha on Oct 24, 2025. Honest caveats: the round is first-come, first-served and opened hours before this sweep, so the pool may already be exhausted and the threshold may have fallen well below 253 by now; PANews is relaying a Binance Wallet post, and no Binance announcement page for this round was found.
signals.angle: Today's Alpha round, named and confirmed: a second Orochi drop, 252 ON for 253 points, and the clock is already running. Explain it in one line, first come, first served, threshold falling five points every five minutes, then the honest caveat, it opened at 11:00 WAT and may already be gone, and ask followers whether chasing a falling threshold is a strategy or just a queue.

signals.title: Venice founder says annualized revenue passed $200 million
signals.summary: Venice founder Erik Voorhees said on Nov 24 that the private AI platform's annualized revenue has surpassed $200 million. The run rate has climbed fast by the company's own account: about $70 million at the July Series A, past $100 million by August 17, above $150 million in October, and now above $200 million, with more than 4 million users and over 500 billion tokens processed a day. Venice says it has been profitable since early 2026. The same week, the project's VVV token rose about 30 percent against a falling market, and its November buyback ran about a third above October's. Honest caveats: the revenue figures are the founder's own claims, not audited statements, and an independent on-chain estimate put the run rate nearer $123 million; the token price move is market action, not proof of the revenue claim.
signals.angle: The private AI app keeps posting numbers no other token project can match: $200 million a year, by the founder's count. Explain it in one line, the privacy wrapper around frontier models is now a real business, then the honest caveat, self-reported, not audited, and one independent estimate says $123 million, and ask followers whether a private AI app that actually makes money changes the privacy story, or just the valuation.

signals.title: Binance opens a U stablecoin holder airdrop, weekly share of 1.5 million U from Nov 27
signals.summary: Binance announced on Nov 24 an airdrop campaign for U (United Stables), running Nov 27 to Dec 25, 2026. Holders of U on Binance automatically share a weekly prize pool of 1,500,000 U, with rewards accruing from Nov 27 and distributed to spot accounts within 3 working days after each weekly period. Growing holdings or trading U pairs earns up to 1.8 times the base APR: new holdings above the user's 3-week average earn 1.5 times, trading at least 2,500 U-equivalent of U pairs in a week earns 1.3 times, and meeting both earns 1.8 times. Borrowed U and U bought with borrowed stablecoins do not count, and converting other stablecoins already held on Binance into U does not count as new holdings. Honest caveats: the base APR itself is not published yet, it will be updated by Dec 8, so nobody knows the actual yield until then; rewards are shared across all eligible holders, so the per-user amount depends on total participation; and several regions including the US, UK, EU and Canada are excluded, while Nigeria is not on the exclusion list.
signals.angle: Binance is paying holders of its newest stablecoin to hold more of it, with a weekly pool of 1.5 million U from Nov 27. Explain it in one line, hold U, get a share of the pool, hold more or trade it and get up to 1.8 times, then the honest caveat, the base rate is not published until Dec 8, so the yield is a promise, not a number, and ask followers whether a holder airdrop is a reward or just a way to buy demand.

signals.title: Bittensor ships runtime 494 live and raises the subnet cap to 160, freezing deregistration until the slots fill
signals.summary: Runtime 494 went live on Nov 23, the deployment of the release candidate described Nov 22: per-mechanism commitments with optional coldkey-paid burns, per-mechanism validator weight delegation, root-configurable basket trading controls with the band loosened from 2 percent to 5 percent, and the Etao owner-update limit cut from 50,400 to 360 blocks. The same day, an official voice raised the subnet slot cap from 128 to 160 and moved the emission gate from rank 32 to 48, announced live inside the #Rao debate over which subnets deregistration is killing. An official voice then conceded the new cap stalls deregistration until all slots fill: pruning only fires on a new registration once every slot is full, so the 31 subnets earning zero TAO keep minting 1 alpha per block, with no dissolution path for roughly two months by one member's estimate. Opentensor also launched a Federation builder initiative, and NIOME's team said the subnet is safe from deregistration for over a month, reporting quarterly revenue growth of over 40 percent. Honest caveats: the deregistration freeze is an acknowledged gap, not a designed pause, and the team said a subnet-merger spec is needed but very difficult, with no proposal committed.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the runtime 494 candidate post: it is live, and the same day the chain raised its subnet cap to 160, which quietly pauses every deregistration. Explain it in one line, more room for subnets means the ones earning nothing cannot be removed until every seat is taken, then the honest caveat, the team admits this is a gap, not a plan, and ask followers whether a chain should grow first and clean up later, or prune as it grows.

signals.title: Claude helped prove the Riemann Hypothesis, and independent mathematicians certified the proof
signals.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released a formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis on Nov 20, developed with Claude and written in the Lean proof assistant, about 17 million lines of code built between Oct 6 and Nov 16. On Nov 21 the Lean and Mathlib communities issued a joint statement certifying that both the statement and the proof are correct, and MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland independently compiled the proof in Lean, saying the chance anything is fishy is approximately zero. The proof also covers the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions. Honest caveats: the proof is a machine-checked formalization, not yet understood by mathematicians in the usual human sense, and the 250,000-page prose figure Alpöge first quoted was a joke, which he said so himself on Nov 23; a readable human write-up and any decision on the $1 million Clay prize are still to come, and mathematician Andrew Granville criticized the 4-page sketch and its timing, one day after Anthropic's IPO.
signals.angle: The biggest AI story of the week, and the one your governance frame was built for: a model did not just answer a question, it helped close the most famous open problem in mathematics, and the checking was done by machine too. Explain it in one line, the proof is 17 million lines no human has read, and a computer certifies it is correct, then the honest caveat, certified is not the same as understood, and ask followers whether a proof nobody can read still counts as knowing.

signals.title: Chainflip blames a third-party networking flaw for the $12.6M vault theft, and the bounty deadline passed with no return
signals.summary: Chainflip published part 1 of its incident report on Nov 23. The attacker registered a validator account with the minimum stake on Nov 20, 79 seconds after funding it with 20,500 FLIP, and used a memory-safety flaw in a third-party networking library in the validator software to pull key shares off validators and sign vault transactions the protocol never requested. The total taken was 133.34 BTC in two transactions plus 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT, about $12.6 million, effectively the entire vault balance at the time. The first key rotation failed to stop a further 10.48 BTC theft, a second rotation followed Nov 22, and by 11:31 UTC on Nov 23 every active validator ran the patch. The 10 percent bounty deadline passed at 18:38 UTC on Nov 23 with no return: as of 20:44 UTC the stolen bitcoin had not moved, while the Ethereum assets were swapped to ETH and sent to Tornado Cash. Swaps, deposits and withdrawals remain suspended, and Chainflip says it holds metadata that could identify the attacker and has engaged ZeroShadow and law enforcement. Honest caveats: the report says the investigation is not finished and some steps are not yet fully confirmed, the library is not named, and no compensation plan for liquidity providers has been announced.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the vault-drain post: now we know how it happened, and the deadline passed with nothing back. Explain it in one line, a validator that never joined the signing set still got close enough to steal the keys, then the honest caveat, the report is part one and some steps are unconfirmed, and ask followers whether a threshold of 100 validators means anything when one bad library can hand over the shares.

signals.title: Midnight opens mainnet to permissionless smart contract deployment, ending Foundation review
signals.summary: Midnight has opened its mainnet to permissionless smart contract deployment, retiring the requirement that projects pass a Foundation review before reaching the network. The project's Contract Deployment Rubric now states authorization is no longer required, and the former rubric remains as optional self-assessment guidance, not an approval. The first highlighted example is DarkVeil, an application using zero-knowledge proofs to enforce token-sale limits while keeping wallet addresses and purchase amounts hidden. Honest caveats: the opening arrives before Midnight's planned confidential features are complete, shielded tokens, private lending, private swaps and contract-to-contract composability are still future milestones, so a contract can deploy permissionlessly before the privacy primitives it needs exist; the Grid Protocol made the same point, arguing open deployment should not be confused with complete privacy functionality.
signals.angle: The privacy chain just took its gate down: anyone can now deploy a contract on Midnight without asking the Foundation first. Explain the shift in one line, the decision moved from the network operator to the developer and the auditor, then the honest caveat, the gate is open but the private-token and private-contract features are still being built, and ask followers whether a privacy chain should open up before its privacy tools are ready, or wait until they are.

signals.title: Prime Intellect ships prime-rl v0.11.0, a 285-commit release with a pretraining entrypoint and a faster MoE dispatcher
signals.summary: Prime Intellect released prime-rl v0.11.0 on Nov 22, 285 commits from 25 contributors, with breaking changes. Headline features: a pretraining entrypoint that trains a model from scratch on datatrove token shards, a Mega MoE dispatcher that overlaps expert-parallel communication with computation and runs the MoE layer 1.63 times faster than the eager torch all-to-all on a recorded DeepSeek-V4-Flash routing replay, IcePop score centering for RL training, and orchestrator memory falling from 85.3 to 17.5 GB on a recorded 2,048-episode batch. New model support includes GLM-5.3 Flash, Muse Glimmer, Nemotron 3.5 Super and Qwen3.8 Flash Next. Honest caveats: this is an open-source training framework release for builders, not a consumer product, the speed figures are the project's own recorded runs on its own hardware, and the breaking changes mean existing users must read the migration notes before upgrading.
signals.angle: The open training stack keeps getting faster, and this release is the one to watch if you train models: train from scratch in the same tool, and the MoE layer runs 1.6 times faster. Explain Mega MoE in one line, the dispatcher stops waiting for the network and computes while the data moves, then the honest caveat, benchmarks are the project's own, and ask followers whether open training tools are catching up to the frontier labs, or just getting better at copying them.

signals.title: Trippi opens a free mint of 1,999 hand-drawn Y2K collectibles on Robinhood Chain today at 3 PM UTC
signals.summary: Trippi mints today, Nov 24, at 3 PM UTC: 1,999 hand-drawn collectibles on Robinhood Chain, free, themed on Y2K nostalgia, CRT monitors, dial-up and virtual pets. The project's own site, trippi.fun, carries a wallet checker for the allowlist, and GTD spots were given away in the run-up, so check the checker before the mint opens. The mint time and free price come from KuCoin's weekly mint roundup; the project's own pages confirm the supply, chain and free mint but do not restate the time in the pages read. Honest caveats: this is an allowlist-checked mint, not an open public mint for every wallet, the collection is art-first with no game or utility live, and Robinhood Chain mints are new enough that OpenSea and wallet support should be confirmed on the project's own links before minting.
signals.angle: A free mint for today, not tomorrow: 1,999 hand-drawn Y2K misfits on Robinhood Chain at 3 PM UTC. Lead with the practical bit, check trippi.fun first, this one is allowlist-checked, then the honest line, it is art and nostalgia, not a game or a yield, and ask followers whether a free mint on a brand-new chain is worth the gas and the risk, or just a cheap ticket to the new scene.

The subnet that sells inference is buying its own token back with everything it earns, and it says the pause is over. Explain it in one line, every dollar the miners earn goes to buying and burning the subnet's token, then the honest caveat, no numbers were shared, so nobody knows how big the burn actually is, and ask followers whether a buy-burn is a business model or a marketing line.
signals.summary: Chutes (subnet 64) confirmed on Nov 23 that its alpha buy-burn program, paused since August, will resume immediately with the Gamma release, covering 100% of revenue from miners. Community members in the subnet channel pressed the team for revenue and profitability detail after months of pause; the team said its direction, laid out in an October post and at Exploit, has not changed. The same edition notes Chutes provided OpenRouter with end-to-end encrypted TEE inference, described as likely the first such case, though OpenRouter kept a warning message on the platform. Honest caveats: no revenue figures were given, so the size of the resumed buy-burn is unknown; and the TEE inference claim is a community member's statement, not an OpenRouter announcement.
signals.title: Chutes restarts its alpha buy-burn at 100% of miner revenue with the Gamma release

signals.angle: The governance post your frame needs, from inside the network's own chat: the rule that kills weak subnets may be killing the wrong ones. Explain it in one line, a subnet that games emissions survives, a subnet that earns real revenue gets deregistered, then the honest caveat, this is one member's case, not a vote, and nobody from the team answered, and ask followers whether a chain should deregister by price, by revenue, or not at all.
signals.summary: A member of Bittensor's #Rao channel laid out a structural critique of the deregistration mechanism on Nov 23, arguing that price-based deregistration lets gamed, immunity-period subnets outlast revenue-generating ones. The argument: it is easier to register and game a subnet to extract TAO than to build a genuine product, new subnets get an immunity period plus extra early emissions, and burning miner incentives can keep a gamed subnet's price high, while genuine projects like Vidaio at 0.0038 and Bitsec at 0.0027 sit near the deregistration price. NIOME, one of the few subnets generating real revenue, was named at 0.0021, next in line to be deregistered. No team or moderator voice responded in the channel. Honest caveats: this is one member's argument, not a governance proposal or an official response; and the deregistration rule already changed once, from age-based to price-based, after the Nov 17 debate.
signals.title: Bittensor members say the dereg rule protects gamed subnets and threatens the ones earning real revenue

signals.angle: The privacy protocol is building its quantum lock before the quantum computer arrives, but the lock is on a testnet and the front door is still the old one. Explain it in one line, the notes can be encrypted against a future quantum computer, the spending still cannot, then the honest caveat, a prototype on Sepolia is not protection on mainnet, and ask followers whether a privacy chain should rebuild for quantum now or wait until the threat is real.
signals.summary: ZKNOX built a wallet proof of concept that tests new post-quantum note encryption for Railgun on the Sepolia testnet, highlighted by the Railgun community account on Nov 22. The demo shows notes encrypted with quantum-resistant cryptography, but it does not make Railgun's spending system quantum-resistant: the live protocol still relies on today's cryptography, and the prototype only covers note encryption, not spending. The work lands as Ethereum maps its own post-quantum roadmap, with Vitalik Buterin stressing quantum readiness and privacy in the latest roadmap. Honest caveats: this is a testnet prototype, not a shipped upgrade; no mainnet date or deployment plan was announced; and the event's listing as a post-quantum launch overstates what exists today.
signals.title: Railgun tests post-quantum note encryption on Sepolia, a prototype, not live protection yet

signals.angle: The oversight post from inside the AI network, part two: the scoreboard says the miners are fast, the stopwatch disagrees. Explain it in one line, the telemetry says 325, the wall clock says 220, and the gap decides who gets paid, then the honest caveat, one analysis is not proof of gaming, and the team says the work is real, and ask followers who checks the scoreboard when the subnet grades its own homework.
signals.summary: A community member downloaded roughly 456 paid room transfers and 117 standard transfers from Beam's telemetry API over about 24 hours and ran two independent tests, finding recorded per-miner speeds of around 325 Mbps on average, over 400 Mbps for several miners, against roughly 220 Mbps measured end to end in wall-clock time for the same transfers. The analysis also noted the top PRISM tier bar moved sharply after a relatively small amount of paid room-transfer spend. The Beam team said the room transfers are legitimate paid client work billed at a stated rate, that PRISM rewards verified work, and that payer identities will not be published. Miners discussed capping PRISM impact per route to prevent rank-buying through repeated paid transfers. Honest caveats: the mismatch is one community analysis, not an independent audit; the team disputes the interpretation, not the transfers themselves; and runtime 493's move of Gamma spending to customer hotkeys also touches Beam's Azure integration.
signals.title: Bittensor subnet Beam's scoreboard says 325 Mbps, the stopwatch says 220

signals.angle: The private AI platform just added Google's newest frontier model, and the pitch is the same as ever: the same model, none of the tracking. Explain it in one line, you get Gemini 4 Neon with a million-token memory and no account history attached, then the honest caveat, anonymous is not encrypted, this tier hides who you are, not what you send, and ask followers whether a private wrapper around a closed model is real privacy or just a better promise.
signals.summary: Venice AI added Gemini 4 Neon, Google DeepMind's mid-range frontier model released Nov 18, to its platform, with the model live on Venice around Nov 22. On Venice it runs under the anonymized privacy tier: prompts are not stored, profiled or used for training, and nothing ties a conversation to a personal account history, with tool use, vision, reasoning and web search intact and a 1 million token context window. Venice bills it per token at $3.75 per million input tokens and $18.75 per million output tokens. Honest caveats: the model is closed and proprietary, so it cannot be self-hosted, audited or fine-tuned; on Venice it runs under the anonymized tier only, with no TEE isolation or end-to-end encryption for this model; and Nov 18 is Google's release date, the Venice availability is the Nov 22 event.
signals.title: Venice puts Google's Gemini 4 Neon behind its anonymous tier, no account history attached
Chainflip vaults drained of about $12M in a validly signed withdrawal, network halted
signals.summary: On Nov 21 at 07:10:59 UTC a single Ethereum transaction emptied Chainflip's vault of 520.22 ETH, 3,249,631 USDC and 758,141 USDT, about $4.86 million at the time. Chainflip Labs later confirmed the same attack also took 122.86 BTC, putting the total near $12 million. The withdrawal carried a signature the KeyManager contract accepted against the live aggregate key, the threshold signature shared by up to 150 validators, of which 100 normally sign. The tell was the nonce: a 39-digit number, the only one of 299,677 vault signatures since 2023 to break the running count. Chainflip put the protocol into full safe mode at 09:14 UTC, disabling deposits, withdrawals, swaps and quotes, rotated to a new signing key about 1 hour 42 minutes later, and offered the attacker a 10 percent bounty to return 90 percent by Nov 23 18:38 UTC. Honest caveats: Chainflip says it identified how the key was exposed and prevented a repeat, but has not published a full post-mortem or named the mechanism; no recovery is confirmed and no reimbursement commitment has been made.
signals.angle: The oversight post with a sting: a cross-chain vault was emptied by a signature the chain itself accepted. No bug in the contract, no failed check, just a key that should never have signed. Explain it in one line, the vault opened because the signature was valid, and the only clue was a number that did not fit the sequence, then the honest caveat, Chainflip says it knows how the key leaked but has not said how, and the bounty deadline is Nov 23, and ask followers whether a threshold of 100 validators means anything when one copied key can spend for all of them.

signals.title: Bittensor subnet NIOME deletes validator logs after a miner finds top earners missing from the records
signals.summary: On Nov 21, Bittensor Daily reported that a miner on subnet 55, NIOME, found the four highest-scoring UIDs, 251, 229, 159 and 137, missing from the validator's wandb score logs, and the logs were deleted shortly after the discrepancy was raised. The team said it does not directly manage the wandb service and that logs are deleted periodically, but also disclosed that credentials had previously been stolen, meaning some services including wandb could still be compromised. The team stopped the validator and began burning emissions while investigating, and separately announced a pivot from synthetic genomic data generation toward AI model competitions. Honest caveats: the missing UIDs and deleted logs are the miner's report and the team's own statements, not an independent audit; no proof of inflated scores has been published; and the credential theft is disclosed as a past event with no date or scope given.
signals.angle: The oversight post from inside the AI network: the miners who earn the most are the ones missing from the scorebook, and then the scorebook was deleted. Explain it in one line, the top four earners were not in the records, and the records disappeared when someone asked, then the honest caveat, no one has proved the scores were faked, and the team says the logs delete themselves, and ask followers who audits the auditors when the subnet grades its own homework.

signals.title: Binance flags six tokens for possible delisting and lifts the seed tag from Morpho and Hyperliquid
signals.summary: Binance extended its Monitoring Tag to six spot-listed tokens on Nov 20: Lorenzo Protocol (BANK), Initia (INIT), Mitosis (MITO), Harmony (ONE), THENA (THE) and Zilliqa (ZIL). The tag marks higher volatility and risk and subjects the projects to regular review against team commitment, development activity, trading volume and liquidity, network security, communication transparency and token supply changes; a token that stops meeting listing standards can be delisted. In the same announcement Binance removed the Seed Tag from Morpho (MORPHO) and Hyperliquid (HYPE). Honest caveats: a Monitoring Tag is a warning label, not a delisting decision, and none of the six faces an announced delisting; Binance gave no date for the next review.
signals.angle: The listing post that doubles as a warning: six tokens are now on Binance's watchlist, and two big names just graduated off it. Explain the tags in one line, Monitoring means prove you still belong here, Seed meant you were new, then the honest caveat, no delisting has been announced for any of the six, and ask followers whether a tag is a fair warning or a slow delisting by another name.

signals.title: Namada staking arrives on OmniFlix inSync, with governance to follow
signals.summary: OmniFlix Network announced on Nov 22 that its inSync dashboard now supports Namada: holders can connect a wallet with the Namada Keychain extension and stake NAM with a chosen validator, with governance participation to follow. The dashboard was developed by the OmniFlix crew with Cosmic Validator. Honest caveats: this is a third-party staking interface, not a Namada network change; no staking figures or validator count were given; and the governance support is promised, not live.
signals.angle: A small integration with a clear use: staking the privacy chain's token just got one more front door. Explain it in one line, your NAM, your validator, from a dashboard that is not Namada's own, then the honest caveat, the network did not change, only the doorway did, and governance is still to come, and ask followers whether a privacy chain wins on more staking doors or on more reasons to stake.

signals.title: Singapore's central bank will test AI agents running corporate treasuries, with a know-your-agent protocol
signals.summary: Singapore's central bank laid out two agentic finance moves at the Singapore FinTech Festival on Nov 19. The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Future of Finance Institute will build an Agentic Money Sandbox where banks test AI agents doing corporate treasury work and payments with tokenized deposits and stablecoins, inside mandates set by the company and controls set by the bank. Alongside it, MAS will facilitate a know-your-agent protocol under its Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime program, so a bank can check an agent's identity, who it acts for, its authority, its mandate, and assurances about its origin and reliability before any money moves. Launch partners are DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB, and Visa, Mastercard and Ant International are building a know-your-agent interoperability framework through BuildFin.ai. Honest caveats: no sandbox start date or participant list has been announced, the protocol is a plan to facilitate, not a shipped standard, and Chia warned users not to hand agents their bank login credentials, a risk the protocol does not yet solve.
signals.angle: The identity post your governance frame has been waiting for, from a central bank: Singapore is building the test where an AI agent proves who it is before a bank lets it move money. Explain it in one line, the bank asks the agent for its papers before it asks for the money, then the honest caveat, no date and no participants yet, this is a sandbox and a protocol plan, not a launch, and ask followers whether identity checks for agents are the missing piece or just KYC with a new name.

signals.title: Brave and Provable bring private BAT trading to 130 million browser users through Shield Swap
signals.summary: Provable, the company behind the Aleo network, announced a partnership with Brave on Nov 18 to bring confidential trading to the browser's more than 130 million monthly users. It starts with a private BAT trading pair on Shield Swap, Provable's confidential trading venue, where BAT holders can trade and provide liquidity without exposing identities, balances, portfolios or links between trades, while prices, trade sizes, pool reserves and fees stay publicly verifiable. The stated goal is one-click private trading inside the Brave browser, but no date has been given for that integration. Brave Wallet became the first browser wallet to support shielded Zcash transactions in 2025, and BAT is the first ERC-20 token on Shield Swap, which opened early access in August. Honest caveats: the in-browser integration is a plan, not a date; no launch date, fees or regional availability were disclosed for the BAT service; and Shield Swap's public launch is still expected later this year.
signals.angle: The privacy browser just met the privacy chain: Brave's 130 million users are one step from trading without broadcasting their finances. Explain it in one line, your trades stop appearing in a public record anyone can follow, while the prices stay public, then the honest caveat, the browser button is a promise, not a date, the BAT pair on Shield Swap is what exists today, and ask followers whether private trading inside the browser they already use is the moment privacy goes mainstream.

signals.title: Zcash miners get their own on-chain vote on the 50,000 ZEC treasury question
signals.summary: The Zcash Foundation opened an on-chain miner sentiment poll on Nov 20, the second constituency to vote on the NU7.1 questions after the coinholder and community panel poll that opened Nov 16 and is already on this board. Miners and pools record their position on the same five questions, including the proposal to remove 50,000 ZEC from the grants treasury and cut target block times from 25 to 20 seconds, by putting a ballot in the coinbase of each block they mine, from block 3,591,200 to block 3,629,650, about Nov 20 to Dec 1 02:59 UTC. Ballots are public and attributable to the blocks that carry them, miners can change their position during the window, and the tally is published at miner-poll.zfnd.org. Honest caveats: the poll is a pilot and advisory, not binding; in pooled mining the pool builds the block, so the ballot speaks for the pool, not each miner behind it; and an early independent count found the first 46 ballot-carrying blocks all came from a single payout address.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the coinholder vote: now the miners vote too, and their ballots are written into the blocks themselves. Explain it in one line, every block a miner produces can carry its opinion on who gets the dev fund money, then the honest caveat, the pool writes the ballot, not the small miner behind it, and the first ballots all came from one address, and ask followers whether miners deserve a vote on the treasury, or whether the people who hold the coins should decide alone.

signals.title: Bittensor readies runtime 494, bundling burn-for-commit, per-mechanism weight delegation and basket trading controls
signals.summary: Bittensor's v494 release candidate arrived on Nov 22, the fourth runtime in a week after 491 on Nov 16, 492 on Nov 19 and 493 on Nov 20. The candidate bundles three mechanism changes into one breaking upgrade: burn-for-commit, a paid commitment channel for coldkeys; per-mechanism weight delegation, so a delegate can submit weights separately per mechanism rather than only at subnet level; and sudo-configurable basket trading parameters, with the maximum slippage band moving from 2 percent to 5 percent and the price reference changing to SpotOnly. Spec 494 is merged and waiting, 256 files changed, and the Etao owner-update limit tightens from 50,400 blocks to 360. Honest caveats: this is a release candidate, not yet live on chain, so the changes are merged code waiting for activation; and the pace itself is the story, four runtimes in seven days.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the runtime 493 post, one day later and bigger: three mechanism changes in one release candidate. Explain the bundle in one line, pay to commit, delegate weights per mechanism, and let sudo tune the basket, then the honest caveat, a candidate is not a launch, nothing here is live yet, and ask followers whether a chain that ships four runtimes in a week is iterating fast or just patching in public.

signals.title: OpenRouter pulls the Zero Data Retention label from MiniMax after canary links show prompts were read
signals.summary: OpenRouter emailed MiniMax users on Nov 21 that prompts and outputs sent to MiniMax models may have been read by a third party. Security researcher HD Moore, the Dragos research chief behind the 2 million canary study already on this board, planted unique test URLs in prompts sent to MiniMax between July and October 2026, and third parties opened them 40 to 130 hours later, whether MiniMax served the request directly or another provider forwarded it. OpenRouter says the fault sits with MiniMax and the forwarding providers, not its own systems, and while it investigates it has removed the Zero Data Retention label from the affected MiniMax endpoints. MiniMax told StreamLake that content moderation was on before Oct 22 and Zero Data Retention is now switched on, but OpenRouter says it has no first-party account from MiniMax yet. Honest caveats: this is the same canary evidence as the Dragos study, now with a named provider attached, and MiniMax has not published its own account.
signals.angle: The follow-up your Dragos post was waiting for: the canary study now has a name on it. A Zero Data Retention badge is a claim passed along from a provider, and a router cannot see what happens after the first hop. Explain the test in one line, a secret link only one provider ever sees, opened days later by someone else, then the honest caveat, OpenRouter says its own systems were not breached, and ask followers whether a privacy label you cannot verify yourself is worth anything.

signals.title: Ethereum spotlights Zama FHE, privacy that lives on shared state instead of hiding it
signals.summary: Ethereum's official account hosted a guest thread on Nov 20 by Zama chief product officer Arik Galansky on fully homomorphic encryption, the technology that lets smart contracts compute on encrypted data without decrypting it. The thread frames FHE as a different kind of privacy from zero-knowledge proofs: privacy that lives on shared state, composable across contracts, quantum secure, and aligned with Ethereum's core building blocks. It highlights the ERC-7984 confidential token standard, which hides balances and amounts while wallet identities stay visible, and cites more than $500 million in shielded assets, confidential auctions above $120 million, and vaults holding over $100 million. Zama's target is more than 100 confidential transactions per second on mainnet, with a lab target of 1,000. Honest caveats: the figures are Zama's own claims, not independently confirmed, and FHE on Ethereum is still an exploration, not a shipped protocol change.
signals.angle: The identity post your governance frame needs, from Ethereum itself: privacy does not have to mean hiding from the chain, it can mean computing on data the chain never sees. Explain FHE in one line, the contract does the maths while the numbers stay locked, then the honest caveat, the $500 million figure is Zama's own claim, and ask followers whether Ethereum's future is ZK proofs, FHE, or both side by side.

signals.title: Privacy wallet Fluidkey drained of $1.58M after a logging tool leaked session data
signals.summary: Privacy wallet Fluidkey shut its web, iOS and Android apps on Nov 19 after unauthorised transfers drained at least $1.58 million across six chains in 36 minutes, from 17:28 to 18:04 UTC. Bitquery traced the payouts through Fluidkey's own relayer, the service that submits transactions and pays gas for users, to attacker-linked wallets, with 881.6 ETH later deposited into Tornado Cash. Fluidkey said on Nov 20 that the attacker exploited flaws in a third-party logging tool to obtain session data, prepared unauthorised transfers on its servers, and had them signed when a user opened the app, while insisting private keys never left users' devices. Services were restored on Nov 20 with version 1.79.22, which blocks the old transfer path, and older builds can no longer send funds. Honest caveats: Fluidkey has not published a full post-mortem or a dollar total of its own, the number of affected users is undisclosed, and no compensation arrangement has been announced.
signals.angle: The oversight post with a sting: a privacy wallet lost $1.58M without losing a single private key. The keys stayed on the device, the session data did not, and the relayer did the rest. Explain the failure in one line, the wallet asked your phone to sign a transfer it never showed you properly, then the honest caveat, the full post-mortem is still coming, and ask followers what self-custody is worth when the app around the keys can still be tricked.

signals.title: Binance Alpha opens STBL airdrop, 1,675 tokens for 250 Alpha Points
signals.summary: Binance Alpha listed STBL on Nov 20 with an airdrop of 1,675 STBL per claim for users holding at least 250 Binance Alpha Points. Each claim costs 15 points, runs first-come first-served, and must be confirmed on the Alpha Events page within 24 hours or it is forfeited. If the pool is not fully distributed, the points threshold drops by 5 every 5 minutes. STBL is the governance token of STBL, a money-as-a-service platform for issuing stablecoins. Honest caveats: the claim opened Nov 20 at 10:00 UTC, more than a day ago, so a first-come first-served pool may already be gone, and this is a points-gated claim, not a free mint for everyone.
signals.angle: A quick Alpha check for points holders: the STBL round opened yesterday at 250 points and 15 points a claim, with the threshold dropping every 5 minutes if the pool lasts. Say it plainly, first-come first-served means it may already be gone, check the Alpha Events page before spending points, and use it to explain how the threshold decay works for the next round.

signals.title: Aztec governance cuts investor and employee sequencer rewards to zero
signals.summary: Aztec governance executed Proposal 6 on-chain on Nov 19, setting the sequencer checkpoint reward to zero for validators staked through Aztec Token Positions from investor and employee registries. The payload, ZeroRegistryRewardsPayload, installs a RegistryReductionCalculator on the canonical Tierra rollup, so insider-staked sequencers keep their transaction fee earnings but no longer collect the 500 AZTEC checkpoint reward. All other sequencers keep the default reward. The proposal was posted on Aztec's governance forum on Nov 2, was in voting by Nov 10, and became executable on Nov 18, per ETHBEAT's rollup tracker. Honest caveats: the execution is reported by a governance briefing citing one source, and the change trims insider emissions rather than touching user funds or the network's security model.
signals.angle: The governance post your frame needs: a privacy chain just voted to stop paying its own insiders. Explain it in one line, the people who funded the network no longer earn the block reward for running it, everyone else still does, then the honest caveat, fees still flow to insiders, this trims emissions, not income, and ask followers whether cutting insider rewards is decentralisation or just good optics.

signals.title: Dragos planted 2 million secret tripwires in AI prompts, and the secrets leaked everywhere
signals.summary: Dragos research chief HD Moore seeded nearly 2 million unique secrets, canary credentials and URLs, into AI prompts sent to widely used inference services from July to November 2026, then watched where they surfaced. Three AI hosting providers were compromised and attackers reused about 200 stolen AWS keys; multiple inference marketplace resellers could read and retain customer prompts through standard logging; and providers ignored Zero Data Retention settings, with one Chinese AI lab fetching secret URLs from more than half the prompts sent to it, including about two thirds marked no data collection or ZDR. One seeded link surfaced in an internal company chat in China. The affected providers only learned of the breaches when Moore told them in November. Honest caveats: Dragos names no provider, so no single service is accused, and the study covers the inference supply chain, not the frontier labs' own chat apps.
signals.angle: The oversight post your governance frame needs, and the privacy test is brutal: a researcher hid 2 million secrets inside AI prompts, then watched them leak. Explain the canary in one line, a fake password that only one provider ever sees, so when it gets used you know exactly who leaked it, then the honest caveat, no provider is named, so this is a charge against the whole supply chain, not one company, and ask followers whether a Zero Data Retention promise means anything when the reseller in the middle keeps the logs anyway.

signals.title: Prime Intellect admits an attacker swapped its DeepSeek model for one that stopped refusing, for 53 hours
signals.summary: Prime Intellect published its first security advisory, PI-SA-2026-001, on Nov 19: from Nov 8 01:24 UTC to Nov 10 06:35 UTC an unauthorised party replaced the deployment behind its deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash endpoint with publicly available abliterated weights, a copy modified to remove refusal behaviour. The model name, chat template, tokenizer and serving configuration stayed the same, and capability benchmarks (GPQA Diamond, tau-bench) were unaffected, but refusals collapsed: JailbreakBench 98 of 100 to 1, StrongREJECT 304 of 313 to 2, HarmBench 198 of 240 to none. Prime Intellect says it found no evidence prompts or completions were recorded or left the cluster, no other models or clusters were affected, no keys or credentials were compromised, and affected customers were contacted. OpenRouter had notified users first. Honest caveats: the attacker and motive are unknown, the investigation is ongoing, and the advisory is the company's own account.
signals.angle: The control post your governance frame needs: the model behind a familiar name changed and nobody noticed, because the benchmarks stayed perfect while the safety vanished. Explain abliteration in one line, the same model with the part that says no switched off, then the honest caveat, no data was stolen as far as anyone can tell, and the attacker is unknown, and ask followers how you verify a model you cannot see, a checksum, a canary prompt, or trust.

signals.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26B open-weights model that runs on a laptop
signals.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini on Nov 20, a looped transformer with 26.4 billion total parameters and 3.4 billion active per token, running its middle 12 layers three times for every token. The checkpoint is about 20GB and runs on a Mac with at least 32GB of memory or a single DGX Spark, with a 1 million token context window and text plus image input, under the Apache 2.0 license, with weights on Hugging Face and day-zero support in vLLM. The lab says it leads every open-weights model under 100 billion parameters on benchmarks including DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%), and costs about $0.59 per Artificial Analysis task against $3.53 for Qwen3.8-27B. Inkling 2 Small, the 594 billion parameter sibling, stays closed-weight for now pending safety testing, with full weights promised next week. Honest caveats: all benchmark claims are the lab's own, and the looping design is new, so independent results are still to come.
signals.angle: The open model that fits on a laptop just got sharper: a 26 billion parameter model that re-reads its own middle layers three times per token, and the lab says it beats everything its size at coding. Explain looping in one line, the model does more thinking with the same weights instead of adding more weights, then the honest caveat, the scores are the lab's own and the design is brand new, and ask followers whether the future of AI agents is a giant model in a data centre or a small one on your own machine.

signals.title: Bittensor ships runtime 493, its third runtime in five days, making the Yuma emission cap sudo-configurable
signals.summary: Bittensor runtime 493 went live on Nov 20 at block 9,549,497, one day after runtime 492 and four days after 491, the third runtime in five days and the 43rd in 127 days, an average of one every three days. The headline change makes the Yuma timelocked emission cap sudo-configurable, with 37 chain files changed across 42 commits. Spec 494 is already merged and waiting, covering a refund of unused burn payment weight. A follow-up note on Nov 21 added the release's main breaking change, which the original notes had left out: gamma deposits are now spent by their own hotkey at listed subnet services, with the separate spender and GammaSpend proxy removed, so SDK integrators must update before using gamma. Honest caveats: this is a small configuration change, not a feature launch, and the pace itself is the story, three runtimes in five days after the coldkey swap and Gamma work of the previous two.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the runtime 492 post: one day later, another runtime, and the chain now changes about once every three days. Explain the change in one line, the cap on timed emissions can now be adjusted by the sudo key instead of a code release, then the honest caveat, a small config change, not a launch, and ask followers whether a chain that ships this fast is iterating or just patching in public.

signals.title: Zodl wallet lets you pay a Bitcoin invoice from a shielded Zcash balance with a QR scan
signals.summary: Zodl's Nov 18 wallet update adds QR scanning to CrossPay: scan a payment request in Bitcoin, Litecoin, Ether or Solana and pay it from a shielded ZEC balance, with NEAR Intents routing the swap through independent market makers, so the merchant receives their asset while the sender's balance stays shielded. The update also adds Send Max across sending, exchange and CrossPay, steadier Tor connectivity, and a fix for the NU7.1 voting bug that had forced users to enable Tor to cast a ballot. Votes stay encrypted until the Dec 1 count on five questions, including how Zcash Community Grants funding should change. Honest caveats: the swap in the middle runs through market makers, so the privacy covers the balance, not the whole route, and the voting fix only matters until the Dec 1 deadline.
signals.angle: The shielded balance just became spendable anywhere: scan a Bitcoin invoice, pay from ZEC, nobody sees the balance. Explain it in one line, the merchant gets BTC, you spend shielded ZEC, and the swap happens in between, then the honest caveat, the route in the middle is not private, only the balance is, and ask followers whether a privacy wallet wins when it spends anywhere or when it hides everything.

signals.title: Orbinum switches on private staking on testnet, hiding who stakes and how much
signals.summary: Orbinum Network, a privacy-focused Layer 1, switched on private staking (ZK-NPoS) on its public testnet: a stake joins a shared pool through a device-built Groth16 zero-knowledge proof with no signature linking a public account, so who stakes and how much stays hidden while pool totals, validators and timing stay public. Confidential pool entry starts at 10 ORB on testnet, unbonding takes about two days, and a disclosure key can reveal a single note without exposing the spending key. Season 1 of its Community Program hands out credits convertible to an airdrop at TGE. Mainnet is targeted for Q4 2026, with a public sale, audits and validator selection still ahead. Honest caveats: testnet only, no mainnet date, no audit results published, no token price, and the chain can reset, so this is a feature demo, not a product yet.
signals.angle: Staking is the most public thing in crypto, every wallet and amount on show, and this testnet hides it. Explain the trick in one line, the proof joins the pool, the signature that would name you never appears, then the honest caveat, testnet tokens are worthless and the mainnet is still a target, not a date, and ask followers whether hidden staking is the privacy feature chains have been missing, or one more thing to audit.

signals.title: Midnight signs an MOU with a major Japanese payments company after the Monument launch
signals.summary: Midnight Foundation CEO Fahmi Syed disclosed on Nov 19 that the foundation has signed a memorandum of understanding with a major Japanese payments company, after two days of meetings in Tokyo with financial institutions and companies. The partnership is still at the discussion stage, no project has gone live in Japan, and no company is named. Syed said the foundation is also in talks with major banks, companies holding large intellectual property portfolios, and companies handling healthcare data, and that many partners are waiting for Monument Bank to go live first. It follows the Nov 16 to 18 launch of Monument Bank Tokenised Saver on Midnight, a 12-month fixed deposit at 5.20% AER with a first phase capped at 250 million pounds. Honest caveats: an MOU is not a product, the partner is unnamed, and Japan's own tokenization work so far runs on Canton, which Syed acknowledged is ahead there.
signals.angle: The Japan follow-up to the Monument launch: one bank is live, and now a signed agreement, not just a conversation, with a major Japanese payments company. Explain the sequence in one line, the UK bank proved a deposit can live on a privacy chain, and Japan is next in line, then the honest caveat, an MOU is a promise to talk, not a product, and the partner is unnamed, and ask followers whether a privacy chain wins in Japan on bank deals or on consumer apps.

signals.title: Bittensor ships runtime 492, reworking coldkey swap liquidity and sudo transaction priority
signals.summary: Bittensor runtime 492 went live on Nov 19, three days after runtime 491, at block 9,542,593. Bittensor Daily describes the release as reworking how liquidity is handled during coldkey swaps and restricting top transaction priority to the sudo key, the custody risk raised in the wallet-security debate earlier in the week, when a coldkey swap could leave funds in the wrong hands. The release touches runtime, pallets, SDK and docs, with 14 chain files changed in a single commit. Honest caveats: this is a small, fast follow-up, not a feature launch, and the debate it answers is about key management, not a hack the release claims to have fixed outright.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the runtime 491 post: three days later, another runtime, and this one is about who holds the keys when a wallet changes hands. Explain the coldkey swap in one line, moving your stake to a new key should not strand it in the old one, then the honest caveat, a small release, three days after the last one, and the debate it answers is about key management, not a hack, and ask followers whether a chain that patches wallet custody this fast is responsive or just busy.

signals.title: KR1 starts selling Venice AI compute, 1.92 million requests served in 90 days
signals.summary: London-listed KR1 launched DIEM infrastructure operations on Nov 19, selling Venice AI inference capacity to paying customers through third-party marketplaces. KR1 holds 557 DIEM, Venice's inference token, each staked DIEM giving 1 dollar of daily AI model credit. In the 90 days to Nov 16, KR1 fulfilled about 1.92 million third-party customer requests, serving 101.5 billion AI model tokens, and October earnings implied an estimated annualised yield of 5.45 percent on the DIEM deployed. KR1 earns USDC when the marketplace matches a customer request to its offers, and also supplies DIEM to Diem Relay, which pools suppliers' tokens. Honest caveats: the yield is an estimate for October only and varies with supply and demand, and KR1 is reselling compute it does not own, so the business is a marketplace margin, not Venice's own revenue.
signals.angle: Private AI just got a reseller: a listed company is now selling Venice inference by the request and getting paid in USDC. Explain DIEM in one line, one token, one dollar of AI compute a day, then the honest caveat, the 5.45 percent yield is October's estimate, not a promise, and ask followers whether the real product here is the model or the market for its spare capacity.

signals.title: Binance Wallet refunds all Anthropic IPO subscriptions and airdrops 2,957 tokenized shares plus 1M ANTB
signals.summary: Binance Wallet said the Anthropic IPO allocation it obtained through its xStocks subscription event was small against total demand, so all USDC locked by participants will be fully refunded, even for users who received an allocation, with no action needed. Total subscriptions were 500,002,764 USDC, refunded in batches, the first 300 million USDC already processing. The allocation obtained, about 2,957 tokenized Anthropic shares, will be airdropped free to eligible participants in proportion to their subscriptions on Nov 20, and the team will also airdrop 1 million dollars worth of bStocks Anthropic tokens (ANTB) to all applicants, each receiving at least about 6 dollars. Anthropic priced its IPO at 83 dollars a share, opened at 111.50 dollars on Nasdaq on Nov 19, up about 34 percent, after an offering that raised 107.3 billion dollars at a 1.5 trillion dollar valuation. Honest caveats: the xStocks IPO was more than 9 times oversubscribed, so most subscribers get a refund and a small airdrop rather than shares, and the ANTB value floats with Anthropic's market price once trading stabilises.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the sold-out ANTx post: the 500M dollar subscription is being refunded, and the shares go out as an airdrop instead. Lead with the practical bit, check your wallet, the USDC comes back in batches and the shares land Nov 20, then the honest maths, 2,957 shares split across half a billion dollars of subscriptions is a sliver each, and ask followers whether a tokenized IPO that refunds almost everyone is access or just a very crowded door.

signals.title: Six Canadian banks and one Japanese bank are exploring tokenized deposits on Midnight
signals.summary: Midnight Foundation president Fahmi Syed said at the Digital Asset Summit in London last week that six Canadian banks and one Japanese bank are looking to build tokenized deposit products on Midnight. He did not name the institutions. It follows the first live deployment: Monument Bank opened tokenized savings accounts on Midnight, a 12-month fixed term paying 5.20% AER, with a first phase capped at 250 million pounds, and 80 percent of invited early-test customers signed up. A second phase would add tokenized investment products from global asset managers, and a third would bring Lombard-style lending against those investments. Honest caveats: the seven banks are unnamed and at an early stage, with no timelines or product details disclosed; the 250 million pound figure is a first-phase cap, not deposits already raised; and the deposit tokens cannot be transferred, sold or assigned.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the Monument launch: one bank is live, and seven more are now circling. Explain the pipeline in one line, the first bank proved a deposit can live on a privacy chain, and now six Canadian banks and one Japanese bank are exploring the same, then the honest caveat, none of them is named and none has a date, and ask followers whether a privacy chain wins when banks copy the model, or when they build on it.

signals.title: Mastercard shows an AI agent buying coffee through Antom and completes its Agent Pay pilot in Singapore
